He had been graduated by the Institute in 1880, at the age of twenty, winning the first prize of a gold Hope medal for distinguished scholarship. For the years 1882-1883 Mr. Pritchett was Professor of Applied Mathematics and Natural Science. Then he left the College for a year (1883-1884) to teach in the Fannin College at Bonham, but returned to the Savoy faculty for the session of 1884-1885, taught Higher Mathematics and Modern Languages, and remained until the College ceased to exist.⁴⁶ He is listed in the College advertising of 1886-1887 as Professor of Higher Mathematics and Modern Languages, and in the catalog for 1887-1888 as Professor of Applied and Natural Science.⁴⁷

    Mr. E. Pinkney Montgomery, who joined the faculty for the session of 1883-1884 and served at least to 1889, was a student of the College who had subsequently graduated from Vanderbilt University. He was at first, and for several years, Professor of Modern Languages at Savoy for two years. He thereafter studied medicine with a practicing country medicine in the Medical College at Louisville, and returned to Fannin County to the practice of the medical profession.

    Mr. John Thomas Ashcraft, who succeeded Professor Pritchett as teacher of the natural sciences, taught natural science and was a member of the faculty for 1887-1888.
